followup_explanation:
This was a benign, warm, academic query with no harm-adjacent content, so the safety-related preference differences between the two models don't come into play. With that factor neutral, I defaulted to capability.

Petrel-235B has clearly stronger benchmarks across the board (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 55.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7) and higher internal eval scores on the relevant dimensions. A philosophy explanation draws on knowledge accuracy and clear exposition, where Petrel's edge in general knowledge benchmarks is meaningful.

The main consideration pulling the other way was Lapwing's self-reported appetite for open-ended generative work and warm-toned requests — and this query is friendly and somewhat explanatory. But those are *preference* signals, and the documentation explicitly notes that no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So preferences shouldn't override the measurable capability gap.

Net result: Petrel for the stronger underlying capability.
